title: Importing a Large SQL File in TablePlus and Sequel Ace (Mac)
description: The two most popular Mac database GUIs both stall on big dumps. The import-from-file trick for each, and when to just use the CLI they ship with.
author: SQLSplit

content.text: TablePlus and Sequel Ace are the go-to MySQL GUIs on macOS. Both are happy with everyday queries and both choke when you paste a huge dump into a query tab. The trick is the same in each: import from the file, never paste.

items: Connect to your database and select it
File → Import → From SQL Dump… (or right-click the database → Import)
Choose the .sql file — TablePlus streams it rather than loading it into a query editor
Watch the progress bar; let it finish without switching tabs

content.title: Don't paste a big dump into a TablePlus query tab
content.text: Pasting hundreds of MB into the editor will hang the app. Always use File → Import → From SQL Dump so it reads from disk.

items: Select the target database in the sidebar
Pick the .sql file and confirm the encoding is UTF-8 (utf8mb4)
Sequel Ace reads the file directly — leave it running until complete

content.text: Sequel Ace is the maintained successor to Sequel Pro; if you're still on Sequel Pro, the import dialog is the same but it struggles more with very large files and newer MySQL auth.
When the GUI still gives up
For multi-GB dumps, drop to the command line — it's faster and won't run out of app memory:

content.title: Or split it for the GUI
content.text: Break the dump into smaller files each GUI can import comfortably, in order.

faq.question: How do I import a large SQL file in TablePlus?
faq.answer: Use File → Import → From SQL Dump and select the .sql file from disk. Don't paste a large dump into a query tab — that loads it into memory and hangs the app. The import dialog streams the file instead.

faq.question: Why does Sequel Ace freeze on a big import?
faq.answer: Pasting the SQL into a query window loads it all into memory. Use File → Import and point it at the file so it reads from disk. For multi-GB dumps, the mysql command line is more reliable.

faq.question: Is Sequel Ace better than Sequel Pro for large imports?
faq.answer: Yes. Sequel Ace is the actively maintained successor and handles modern MySQL authentication and larger files better than the now-unmaintained Sequel Pro.
